chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a freedwoman whom my brother had emancipated, and she had been serving the female slaves and was among his dependents, so he instructed me to spend on her from the middle [of the maintenance], so he said: 'If she is with the female slaves and remains with them, then spend on her and follow his instruction.'

key_terms.مُحَرَّرَةٍ: A female slave who has been partially or fully emancipated

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on maintaining a freed slave woman who remains in the household after her owner's death?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the implementation of a testator's specific bequest for a freed slave woman who remains in the household, emphasizing the binding nature of honoring the deceased's wish regarding her maintenance level. It highlights the Shia legal principle that the deceased's directive for 'middle-tier' spending (al-wasat) takes precedence when the woman continues to reside with the family's female servants, ensuring her dignity and financial security post-emancipation. This ruling underscores the importance of fulfilling testamentary instructions within the framework of Islamic inheritance law, particularly regarding those who transition from servitude to freedom while remaining under the family's care.
